name: Saint John of Sahagún
history: A Spanish priest, called John of San Facundo after his birthplace, who became an Augustinian friar and the great preacher of Salamanca. In a city torn by feuds between noble families he worked tirelessly to make peace. He was known for his long, devout celebration of Mass and for the frankness of his preaching. He is the patron of Salamanca.
life: John González de Castrillo was born at Sahagún in the kingdom of León and studied at the University of Salamanca. Ordained priest, he held several benefices but gave them up to live simply and preach. In 1463 he entered the Augustinian friars at Salamanca. The city was then divided by violent rivalry between two factions of nobles, and John, preaching and visiting both sides, brought many to reconciliation. He spoke plainly against injustice and the vices of the powerful, which won him enemies. He celebrated Mass slowly and with great recollection, and his brothers believed he was granted a vision of Christ at the altar. Tradition holds that he died after being poisoned by a woman whose lover he had converted. He was canonised in 1690.
prayerTo: Saint John of Sahagún, peacemaker of Salamanca, you went between enemies with nothing but the Gospel. Pray for families and communities divided by old quarrels, for preachers who must speak hard truths, and for me, that I may love the Mass and work for peace where I live. Amen.
penance: Take a first step today towards healing a quarrel, your own or one you can help with, and arrive early for Mass to pray quietly beforehand.
meditation: Blessed are the peacemakers. Is there a feud near you that you have simply accepted?
prayer: O God, author of peace and lover of charity, Who endowed blessed John, Your Confessor, with a wondrous grace for reconciling enemies; grant by his merits and intercession, that, being ourselves firmly rooted in Your charity, we may not be separated from You by any temptations. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
